title: Monolith First
summary: Martin Fowler (2015): successful microservice systems grew out of monoliths while greenfield microservice systems mostly ran into trouble, so start with a monolith and split once boundaries are understood.

assertions.quote: you should build a new application as a monolith initially, even if you think it's likely that it will benefit from a microservices architecture later on
Almost all the cases where I've heard of a system that was built as a microservice system from scratch, it has ended up in serious trouble.
Any refactoring of functionality between services is much harder than it is in a monolith.
Most systems acquire too many dependencies between their modules, and thus can't be sensibly broken apart.

verdicts.note: Consistent with migration case studies, though some decompositions of tangled code succeeded with heavy investment.
